requirements.text: The SLD shall be designed and constructed so that an N3 goods vehicle in normal use, despite the vibrations to which it may be subjected, still limits its maximum speed in accordance with UN R89 Part I.
The SLD shall be designed, constructed and assembled to resist corrosion and ageing phenomena to which it may be exposed and to resist tampering.
The SLD shall lock the set speed Vset so that it cannot be increased or removed, temporarily or permanently, on vehicles in use.

The SLD and its operating connections, except those essential for running the vehicle, shall be capable of being protected from unauthorised adjustment or interruption of energy supply by seals and/or special tools.
The SLD shall not actuate the vehicle's service braking system, and any retarder output shall operate only after the device has restricted the fuel feed to the minimum fuel position.
The SLD shall not affect the vehicle's road speed when a positive action on the accelerator is applied while the vehicle is running at its set speed.
The SLD shall allow normal accelerator control to be used for gear changing.
The SLD shall be designed so that no malfunction or unauthorised interference results in engine power above that demanded by the driver's accelerator position.
The SLD shall operate satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment without causing unacceptable electromagnetic disturbance to anything in that environment.
The SLD shall be tested to the speed limitation tests and performance requirements of Annex 5 of UN R89.

The SLD shall be evaluated by accelerating the vehicle from 10 km/h below the set speed with a fully positive action on the accelerator, maintaining the action at least 30 seconds after stabilisation.
The SLD shall limit the stabilised speed so that Vstab does not exceed Vset, allowing a tolerance of 5% of Vset or 5 km/h, whichever is greater.
The SLD shall ensure that, after the stabilised speed is first reached, Vmax does not exceed Vstab by more than 5%.
The SLD shall attain the stabilised speed conditions within 10 s of first reaching Vstab.
The SLD shall hold the vehicle speed within 4% of Vstab or 2 km/h, whichever is greater, when stable speed control has been achieved.
The SLD shall keep the rate of change of speed below 0.2 m/s2, measured over a period greater than 0.1 s, when stable speed control has been achieved.
The SLD shall meet the acceleration test acceptance criteria in each gear ratio that could theoretically allow the set speed to be exceeded.
The SLD shall, in the steady speed test method, keep Vstab on each test run within Vset plus a tolerance of 5% of Vset or 5 km/h, whichever is greater.
The SLD shall produce stabilisation speeds in the steady speed test that differ by no more than 3 km/h between test runs.
The SLD shall complete 50,000 endurance cycles at an ambient temperature of 20 °C ± 2 °C.
The electronic components of the SLD shall complete 12,500 endurance cycles in a climatic chamber maintained at 65 °C ± 5 °C.
The mechanical components of the SLD shall complete 12,500 endurance cycles in a climatic chamber maintained at 100 °C ± 5 °C.
The SLD shall complete 12,500 endurance cycles in a climatic chamber maintained at -20 °C ± 5 °C.
SLD components exposed to the ambient road environment shall complete 12,500 endurance cycles in a salt atmosphere chamber with 5% sodium chloride at 35 °C ± 2 °C.
The SLD, mounted as on the vehicle, shall withstand a sinusoidal vibration test over 10–24 Hz at ± 2 mm amplitude in all three planes.
The SLD shall withstand a sinusoidal vibration test over 24–1,000 Hz at 2.5 g for chassis- and cab-mounted components and 5 g for engine-mounted components.
The SLD shall show no modification of its performance with regard to the set speed at the end of the endurance tests.

The SLD shall retain its effectiveness when exposed to magnetic or electric fields, demonstrated by fulfilling UN Regulation No. 10 (03 series of amendments for vehicles without a charging coupling system).
The SLD ECU, as an ESA, shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz and 63 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz for broadband radiated emissions when measured per Annex 7.
The SLD ECU, as an ESA, shall not exceed 52 to 42 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz and 53 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz for narrowband radiated emissions when measured per Annex 8.

The SLD ECU shall withstand, in over 90% of the 20–6,000 MHz band, immunity test levels of 60 V/m (stripline), 75 V/m (TEM cell), 60 mA (BCI), 30 V/m (ALSE) and 21 V/m (reverberation chamber) below 2 GHz.
The SLD ECU shall withstand the minimum test levels of 50 V/m (stripline), 62.5 V/m (TEM cell), 50 mA (BCI), 25 V/m (ALSE) and 18 V/m (reverberation chamber) over the whole 20–6,000 MHz band.
The SLD shall show no degradation of its speed-limitation function, as an immunity related function, during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.
The SLD ECU on the 24 V supply shall pass ISO 7637-2 test pulses 1 (-450 V, 500 pulses, FPSC III) and 2a (+37 V, 500 pulses, FPSC I) for immunity related functions.
The SLD ECU on the 24 V supply shall pass pulses 2b (+20 V, 10 pulses, FPSC II), 3a (-150 V, 1 h, FPSC I) and 3b (+150 V, 1 h, FPSC I) applied to the supply lines.
The SLD ECU shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile with 10 pulses at functional status classification II, since it must be operational during engine start phases.
The SLD ECU, being related to immunity related functions, shall achieve functional status B for the starting profile on the 24 V system.
The SLD shall support identification and management of supplier-related cyber security risks for the vehicle type on which it is installed.

The SLD, as a critical element of the vehicle type, shall be subject to an exhaustive cyber security risk assessment covering its elements, their interactions and its interactions with external systems.
The SLD shall implement proportionate mitigations against the cyber security risks identified in the risk assessment, including all relevant mitigations of Annex 5, Parts B and C.

The SLD shall apply security controls to its external interfaces, including the calibration and diagnostic connector and the CAN/speed sensor interfaces, to prevent code injection and unauthorised parameter manipulation.
The SLD shall apply access-control techniques and designs to protect the stored set speed, calibration data and fault-event records from unauthorised change or deletion.
The SLD shall verify the authenticity and integrity of messages it receives over its vehicle network interfaces before acting on them.
The SLD shall implement measures to detect malicious internal messages or activity on the vehicle network that could affect the speed limitation function.
The SLD shall include measures to detect and prevent cyber-attacks against the vehicle, and to provide data forensic capability enabling analysis of attempted or successful attacks.
The SLD shall be subjected to appropriate and sufficient testing, prior to type approval, to verify the effectiveness of its implemented cyber security measures.
Any cryptographic module used in the SLD for tamper detection or message authentication shall be in line with consensus standards, or its use shall be justified.
